title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI
talk_summary: Laurie Voss argues that AI has made code generation cheap but human review is now the bottleneck, and that review must be rebuilt as an engineered system (multi-pass reviewers, rubrics, evals, production telemetry) rather than skipped. The data shows automated reviewers still miss mergeability, regressions, and are fooled by confidently-framed bad code, so humans move up the stack to designing and tuning the review harness.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run several independent review passes over the same diff (shuffling reviewer order) and keep only findings that multiple passes agree on, to suppress false positives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Run several review passes, see keep what they agree on... it review raised review quality by up to 44%.
takeaways.numbers: Cursor ran 8 review passes; Peking University study: up to 44% review quality improvement; Cursor resolution rate 52% -> 70%+

takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly instruct the reviewer model to distrust the code by default and assume something is wrong, because models otherwise rubber-stamp diffs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they had to tell it don't trust the code by default. Assume there is something wrong with it.

takeaways.technique: Reviewer spawns a fix agent (review fused with repair)
takeaways.what_they_do: The reviewer, on finding a bug, spawns a fix agent that writes a patch and returns a diff for approval instead of just flagging.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Cursor's reviewer now spawns a fix agent from its own findings. So it doesn't just flag the bug. uh it writes a patch

takeaways.technique: Codify a mergeability rubric as machine-checkable evals
takeaways.what_they_do: Frontier Code grades behavioral correctness, regression, safety, scope discipline, test quality, maintainability — a human review rubric made machine-checkable; models score far lower on it than on test-passing benchmarks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Frontierbench grades behavioral correctness, regression, safety, scope discipline, test quality, and maintainability. This is a human review rubric uh made machine checkable.
takeaways.numbers: Fable 5: 88% SWE-bench Pro vs 29% on hardest Frontier Code slice; GPT 5.5 under 6%

takeaways.technique: Production trajectory as the last reviewer
takeaways.what_they_do: Once pre-merge review is machine-driven, watch what the code actually does in production step-by-step (trajectories), not just test pass/fail.
takeaways.evidence_quote: once the premerge review is all machines watching what the code actually does becomes the last reviewer standing.

takeaways.technique: Treat automated reviewers as prompt-injectable; gate trusted inputs
takeaways.what_they_do: Anthropic's security reviewer README warns it is not hardened against prompt injection and should only review trusted PRs; studies show confidently-framed bad code fools agents 88% vs 35% for humans.
takeaways.evidence_quote: vulnerable code dressed up in an innocent commit message uh fooled an autonomous review agent in 88% of attempts.
